notes.summary: Covers team sizes, trophies and the sports they belong to, sports terminology, field measurements, Olympic and Asian Games history, and India's landmark sporting achievements. SSC CGL asks short factual one-liners such as 'X Cup is related to which sport', 'how many players', 'the term Y belongs to', and India's Olympic firsts.
keyPoints: Players per side on field/court: volleyball 6, basketball 5, kabaddi 7, kho-kho 9, polo 4, water polo 7, netball 7; cricket, football and hockey 11.
Football trophies: Durand Cup (started 1888), Santosh Trophy, Subroto Cup. Cricket: Ranji, Duleep, Irani. Hockey: Aga Khan Cup, Beighton Cup.
International team trophies: Thomas Cup (men) and Uber Cup (women) – badminton; Davis Cup – tennis; Ryder Cup – golf; Stanley Cup – ice hockey.
Measurements: cricket pitch 22 yards (about 20.12 m); marathon 42.195 km; chessboard 8 × 8 = 64 squares; shuttlecock has 16 feathers.
Terms: googly, LBW, maiden over – cricket; snatch, clean and jerk – weightlifting; checkmate, castling – chess; love, deuce, ace – tennis; penalty corner – hockey.
Olympics: first modern Games – Athens 1896; ring colours blue, yellow, black, green, red on white. First Asian Games – New Delhi 1951. First FIFA World Cup – Uruguay 1930.

India's Olympic firsts: Abhinav Bindra – first individual gold (Beijing 2008, 10 m air rifle); Neeraj Chopra – first athletics gold (Tokyo Games held in 2021, javelin, 87.58 m); Karnam Malleswari – first Indian woman medallist (Sydney 2000, weightlifting bronze).
Nicknames: Milkha Singh – Flying Sikh; P. T. Usha – Payyoli Express; Dhyan Chand – The Wizard; Kapil Dev – Haryana Hurricane.
India won the ODI Cricket World Cup in 1983 (Kapil Dev) and 2011 (M. S. Dhoni).
traps: Thomas Cup is for men and Uber Cup for women in badminton — don't swap them.
Aga Khan Cup is hockey, not cricket; Durand Cup is football, not polo or hockey.
The cricket pitch is 22 yards, not 22 metres.
A marathon is 42.195 km; 26.2 is the figure in miles and 21.0975 km is a half marathon.
Rajyavardhan Rathore won silver in 2004; the first individual Olympic gold was Abhinav Bindra's in 2008.
notes.examTip: Revise a two-column trophy–sport and term–sport list the night before; these questions take seconds and need no calculation, so answer them first.

questions.text: How many players from each team are on the court at a time in a game of volleyball?
questions.explanation:
A volleyball team has 6 players on court – three in the front row and three in the back row.
Basketball has 5, kabaddi has 7 and kho-kho has 9 on the field, which are the common mix-ups.
Answer: 6.

questions.text: Which Indian athlete is popularly known as the 'Flying Sikh'?
questions.explanation:
Milkha Singh was given the title 'Flying Sikh' after winning a race in Lahore in 1960; he finished fourth in the 400 m at the 1960 Rome Olympics.
The other options have their own nicknames: Dhyan Chand – 'The Wizard', P. T. Usha – 'Payyoli Express', Kapil Dev – 'Haryana Hurricane'.
Answer: Milkha Singh.

questions.text: How many squares are there on a standard chessboard?
questions.explanation:
A chessboard is an 8 × 8 grid.
8 × 8 = 64 squares, 32 light and 32 dark.
Each player starts with 16 pieces.
Answer: 64.

questions.text: The Durand Cup, one of the oldest tournaments of its kind in Asia, is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation:
The Durand Cup was first held in 1888 and is named after Sir Mortimer Durand, then Foreign Secretary of British India.
It is a football tournament and among the oldest football competitions in the world.
Other Indian football trophies include the Santosh Trophy and the Subroto Cup.
Answer: Football.

questions.text: The terms 'snatch' and 'clean and jerk' are associated with which sport?
questions.explanation:
Olympic weightlifting has two lifts.
In the snatch, the bar is raised overhead in one continuous movement.
In the clean and jerk, it is first lifted to the shoulders and then jerked overhead.
A lifter's total is the best snatch plus the best clean and jerk.
Answer: Weightlifting.

questions.text: What is the length of a cricket pitch between the two sets of stumps?
questions.explanation:
Under the Laws of Cricket, the pitch is 22 yards (about 20.12 m) long between the two sets of stumps and 10 feet wide.
'22 metres' is a trap – the unit is yards, not metres.
Answer: 22 yards.

questions.text: Who became the first Indian to win an individual Olympic gold medal?
questions.explanation:
Abhinav Bindra won gold in the men's 10 m air rifle at the 2008 Beijing Olympics – India's first individual Olympic gold.
Rathore won silver in double trap (2004) and Leander Paes won bronze in tennis (1996).
Neeraj Chopra's javelin gold came later, at the Tokyo Games.
Answer: Abhinav Bindra.

questions.text: At the Tokyo Olympics (held in 2021), Neeraj Chopra won India's first-ever Olympic gold medal in athletics. In which event?
questions.explanation:
Neeraj Chopra won the men's javelin throw final with a best throw of 87.58 m.
It was India's first Olympic gold in track and field and its second individual Olympic gold after Abhinav Bindra (2008).
Answer: Javelin throw.

questions.text: What is the official distance of a marathon race?
questions.explanation:
The marathon distance comes from the 1908 London Olympics course and was standardised in 1921 at 42.195 km (26 miles 385 yards).
26.2 is the approximate distance in miles, not kilometres.
21.0975 km is exactly half – a half marathon.
Answer: 42.195 km.

questions.text: Which of the following trophy–sport pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
questions.explanation:
Uber Cup is the women's world team championship in badminton – correct.
Ryder Cup is a golf contest between Europe and the USA – correct.
Stanley Cup is awarded in professional ice hockey – correct.
The Aga Khan Cup is a hockey tournament, not cricket.
Answer: Aga Khan Cup – Cricket.

questions.text: The first Asian Games were held in 1951 in which city?
questions.explanation:
The inaugural Asian Games were held in New Delhi in March 1951.
The next editions went to Manila (1954), Tokyo (1958) and Jakarta (1962), so the other options are later hosts.
New Delhi hosted the Games again in 1982.
Answer: New Delhi.
